resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 supported. Aramco's June/July 2024 $25bn gas-expansion announcement (Saudi Press Agency N2131194, official) states the MGS Phase 3 expansion will raise capacity by an additional 3.15 bscfd 'by 2028' via ~4,000 km of pipelines and 17 compression trains; corroborated by World Oil (independent trade). Project trackers (DMS Projects, OGN) independently list Package 8 (EWPS-8 to EWPS-10) construction begun 2Q-2024 with completion by 4Q-2028 — an independent surface for the 2028 date. Original Aramco.com URL times out to the verifier (live but bot-blocked); Wayback copy OK.

CONTRADICTION FLAG: no source found stating 190 km for this segment. Package 8 (EWPS-8 to EWPS-10) is described across OGN and DMS Projects as 'laying of 56-inch east-west gas pipelines 3 and 4 from EWPS-8 to EWPS-10, covering a distance of 480 km' — i.e. two parallel 56-inch lines totaling 480 km (~240 km per line), not 190 km. Pipeline Technology Journal reports L&T completed a 120 km stretch of the package. GEM's row is line '4' of the pair; the stated 190 km is not corroborated by any located source and conflicts with the ~240 km/line implied by the 480 km two-line figure. Left UNRESOLVED pending a source that states the per-line 190 km, or a value revision.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia supported. DMS Projects Package 8 page (EWPS-8 to EWPS-10 pipeline) lists Country: Saudi Arabia; Aramco/SPA announcement describes the Master Gas System as the domestic Saudi network delivering gas to customers across the Kingdom. Both endpoints (EWPS = East-West Pipeline Stations 8 and 10) are internal Saudi Master Gas System stations, so the line is wholly within Saudi Arabia.

Owner1=Aramco 100% supported. DMS Projects Package 8 page lists Owner: Saudi Aramco. The Master Gas System is wholly owned and operated by Saudi Aramco, which awarded the Phase 3 EPC contracts (SPA/Aramco announcement, World Oil). No JV or third-party equity indicated for the pipeline itself.
